title: One clique vertex per clause
statement: Let $f$ be a 3-CNF formula with $m$ clauses, and let $s$ be a set of vertices of the conflict graph of $f$. Suppose that $s$ has exactly $m$ elements and forms a clique, meaning any two distinct vertices of $s$ are adjacent. Then for every clause index $i \in \mathrm{Fin}\,m$ there is exactly one vertex $u \in s$ whose clause component equals $i$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a 3-CNF formula with m = f.length clauses
s is a finite set of conflict-graph vertices
s has cardinality equal to the number of clauses m
s is a clique in the conflict graph of f
replaced:
If $s$ is a set of $m$ vertices forming a clique in the conflict graph of a formula
$f$ with $m$ clauses, then for every clause index $i : \mathrm{Fin}\,m$ there is
exactly one vertex $u \in s$ with $u.c\_idx = i$.
